title: Epodi
author: Q. Horatius Flaccus
notes: Epode 5 and 17: Canidia the witch — canonical Roman literary magic, love potions, necromancy

title: Belli Civilis Liber VI
author: M. Annaeus Lucanus
notes: The Erichtho episode (ll.507-830): most detailed necromancy scene in classical Latin

title: Belli Civilis Liber I
author: M. Annaeus Lucanus
notes: Opening book with omens, prodigies, portents before the civil war

title: Metamorphoseon Liber I
author: L. Apuleius Madaurensis
notes: Book I: Lucius arrives in Thessaly, tales of witchcraft, Meroe transforms traveler

title: Metamorphoseon Liber II
author: L. Apuleius Madaurensis
notes: Book II: Pamphile the witch, Lucius witnesses transformation, Thelyphron's tale

title: Metamorphoseon Liber III
author: L. Apuleius Madaurensis
notes: Book III: Lucius transformed into an ass by Pamphile's magical ointment

title: Metamorphoseon Liber XI
author: L. Apuleius Madaurensis
notes: Book XI: Isis apparition, initiation into mysteries, Lucius restored — central text of religious magic

title: De Deo Socratis
author: L. Apuleius Madaurensis
notes: Doctrine of intermediate daemons between gods and men — foundational for Agrippa and Renaissance demonology

title: Apologia sive Pro se de Magia
author: L. Apuleius Madaurensis
notes: Defense against charges of using magic — priceless document of Roman attitudes to magia

title: Aeneidos Liber IV
author: P. Vergilius Maro
notes: Dido's funeral pyre as magic ritual (ll.474-521), cursing Aeneas — canonical magic in the Aeneid

title: Aeneidos Liber VI
author: P. Vergilius Maro
notes: Descent to the underworld: the Golden Bough, Sibyl, Hecate, the dead — most influential Latin katabasis

title: Metamorphoseon Liber VII
author: P. Ovidius Naso
notes: Medea's incantation and herb-gathering (ll.179-293) — the fullest Latin account of witchcraft ritual

title: Metamorphoseon Liber XIV
author: P. Ovidius Naso
notes: Circe's magic, Picus transformed — Circe as archetype of the learned witch

title: Annalium Liber II
author: P. Cornelius Tacitus
notes: Annals 2: Germanicus's death by magic (defixiones, leaden tablets) — famous Roman magic trial

title: De Civitate Dei Liber VIII
author: Aurelius Augustinus
notes: Book 8: Demons as intermediaries (against Apuleius), Platonist demonology vs. Christianity

title: De Civitate Dei Liber X
author: Aurelius Augustinus
notes: Book 10: Theurgy, Porphyry, true vs. false worship of intermediaries — key anti-theurgic text

title: Ecloga VIII
author: P. Vergilius Maro
notes: Alphesiboeus's magic spell (Amaryllis draw-him-home ritual) — model for all Latin erotic magic

title: Ecloga I
author: P. Vergilius Maro
notes: First Eclogue — pastoral framing, dispossession; precedes the magic eclogues

title: Amorum Liber III
author: P. Ovidius Naso
notes: Amores III.7 (impotence curse), III.3 (perjury and love magic in Roman elegy)

title: Amorum Liber I
author: P. Ovidius Naso
notes: Amores Book I — elegiac love, early magic references

title: De Divinatione Liber Prior
author: M. Tullius Cicero
notes: Book I: Quintus defends divination — Stoic arguments for signs, omens, dreams, oracles

title: De Divinatione Liber Alter
author: M. Tullius Cicero
notes: Book II: Cicero refutes divination — Academic skepticism, rational critique of sortilege

title: Naturalis Historia Liber I
author: C. Plinius Secundus
notes: Book I: Preface and table of contents — Pliny's encyclopedic scope, frequently cited in magic tradition

title: Medea
author: L. Annaeus Seneca
notes: Medea's magic monologue (Act IV) — most elaborate dramatic incantation in Latin, cited by Renaissance magicians

title: Etymologiarum Liber VIII
author: Isidorus Hispalensis
notes: Book 8 ch.9: De Magis — systematic classification of magic types; canonical medieval taxonomy

title: De Rerum Natura Liber I
author: T. Lucretius Carus
notes: Book I: materialist cosmology — atoms, void, anti-providential; the anti-magical foil for Renaissance Platonists

title: De Rerum Natura Liber III
author: T. Lucretius Carus
notes: Book III: on the soul — mortality argument, against fear of death; anti-necromantic

title: Astronomica Liber I
author: M. Manilius
notes: Book I: poetic astrology — zodiac, planets, their natures; key for astrological magic

title: Astronomica Liber II
author: M. Manilius
notes: Book II: signs, decans, dodecatemoria; elaborates astrological influence doctrine

title: Astronomica Liber IV
author: M. Manilius
notes: Book IV: zodiacal influences on human character — horoscopic astrology, paranatellonta

title: Satira VI
author: D. Iunius Iuvenalis
notes: Satire 6: women and magic — astrologers, Chaldaeans, exorcists, poisoners in imperial Rome

title: De Natura Deorum Liber I
author: M. Tullius Cicero
notes: Book I: Epicurean theology — gods as non-interventionist; Stoic and Academic views on divine nature

title: De Natura Deorum Liber II
author: M. Tullius Cicero
notes: Book II: Stoic theology — providential universe, divination as consequence; key for Cicero on natural theology

title: Fastorum Liber I
author: P. Ovidius Naso
notes: Fasti Book I: January ritual calendar — Janus, Lemuralia precursors, Roman religious magic

title: Fastorum Liber V
author: P. Ovidius Naso
notes: Fasti Book V: Lemuralia (May 9,11,13) — exorcism ritual for domestic ghosts (lemures)

title: Annalium Liber IV
author: P. Cornelius Tacitus
notes: Annals IV: astrologers and magic practitioners prosecuted under Tiberius

title: Oedipus
author: L. Annaeus Seneca
notes: Oedipus — Tiresias divination scene, Laius's ghost raised; major necromancy and divination text

title: Naturalis Historia Praefatio
author: C. Plinius Secundus
notes: Preface — Pliny's dedicatory epistle to Vespasian, scope of the work; cited in all natural magic literature

title: Belli Civilis Liber V
author: M. Annaeus Lucanus
notes: Book V: Appius consults the Delphic oracle — divination scene before Pharsalus

title: De Mundo
author: L. Apuleius Madaurensis
notes: De Mundo — Apuleius's adaptation of Pseudo-Aristotle's cosmology, daemons as world-governors

title: Remedia Amoris
author: P. Ovidius Naso
notes: Remedies for Love — counter to love magic, herbalism for unlove; Ovid as both magician and anti-magician

title: Georgicorum Liber I
author: P. Vergilius Maro
notes: Georgics Book I: omens, weather-signs, prodigies; agricultural divination and natural magic

title: Thyestes
author: L. Annaeus Seneca
notes: Thyestes — Tantalus summoned from underworld, necromancy opening, Atreus's forbidden feast

title: Etymologiarum Liber IX
author: Isidorus Hispalensis
notes: Book 9: Languages and peoples — Hebrew as divine language, Babel, linguistic taxonomy

title: Confessionum Liber VII
author: Aurelius Augustinus
notes: Confessions VII: Augustine reads the Platonists — vision of God, the soul's ascent, pride of Neoplatonism

title: Carminum Liber III
author: Q. Horatius Flaccus
notes: Odes III — III.13 Fons Bandusiae (spring ritual); III.4 Muses/Fate; various ritual and religious themes
